genericProblem: A P6-2 change can appear locally complete while owner truth, user-facing preconditions, independent adversarial coverage, and required execution reporting have not been closed as one finite delivery unit.
finiteDenominator: platform administrator bounded paging and owner authorization/receipt command families
selected-workspace task entrypoints across organization, contract, workspace-IAM, extension and audit owners
the six platform WorkspaceScope consumer paths and the one PlatformApp shell host
extension first-configuration receipt claim/replay, five business object catalog rows, and strict operations lookup
every material P6-2 implementation action: pre/post hook, independent review lane, and six-line active-goal progress report
counterexamples: Operations extension reads and writes retain strict requireDefinition; management-only readback must not weaken them.
Asset receipt creation stages an asset before its receipt and is not an extension first-configuration counterexample.
A shell-owned React Context is permitted; Redux slice/store expansion is not.
Selected groupWorkspaceKey is a locator/context prerequisite, not a frontend authorization decision.

findings.evidence: Platform administrator list must use owner-bounded paging rather than an edge approximation.
Owner commands must recheck enabled platform-super-admin authority.
Workspace account and role commands require owner-local receipt replay.
Selected-workspace reads require owner enabled-workspace resolution.

The platform workspace selector was duplicated into six pages, silently selected items[0], and was absent from the required side-bar footer; IA-02/IA-03 require one explicit shell-owned selection and no task read before selection.

The extension first-configuration path has receipt-before-create ordering, owner-generated opaque keys, five fixed business objects, and an unconfigured state; testing only one failure at a time concealed the full closure denominator.
Active P6-2 work did not consistently use the mandated parallel independent audit and exact six-line progress format, so execution governance itself was not demonstrably closed.

A stale CURRENT_* authorization record was treated as a new request for Dexter approval even though Dexter had already granted full P6 authority; the correct remedy is control-plane alignment by Codex, not repeated authorization interruption.

Treating the approved page-control and interaction comparison as a post-L2 review allowed L2 to become a substitute for fidelity. The finite denominator is every UI-bearing delivery's approved interaction artifact, physical screen contract, implemented page/control and planned L2 case; comparison must admit L2, not follow it.

A prose instruction to read IA before implementation did not prevent source-first UI work. The reusable failure mode is no fail-closed proof that each first-written UI consumer was bound to the approved IA and physical contract.
